text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The state drug control authority has asked hospitals and pharmacies to immediately withdraw a batch of gammaglobulin because one of the donors for the blood plasma was infected with Creutzfeldt-Jakobs disease. Manufacturer of the blood plasma, Swiss drug group Novartes, sent an advisory to the authority on Friday.

- Many top politicians are sceptical to claims by the outgoing security chief, Ellen Holager Andenaes, that espionage against Norway in 1997 has increased to the same level of activity as before the fall of the Berlin Wall.

- Politicians on Tuesday night held the first televised debate with a live audience in this year's election campaign. The debate was on tax and duties policy, but the politicans fear that voters understand few of the issues.
- In a new national survey, one in four 14-year-olds says they have psychological problems, problems with their teachers, fellow students and parents, or at they have physical pains.

- More than 500 companies are represented at fish-farming fair, Aqua Nor 97, which opens in Trondheim today. Fish farmers, producers, researchers and deliverers from across the world will be represented and the fair is expected to attract 20-25,000 visitors.

- Lower-than-expected results at Norway Seafoods ASA sent the share price down by 20 percent on the Oslo Bourse on Tuesday. Only three months after private investor Kjell Inge Roekke resigned as head of the company, the food producer posted a pre-tax deficit of 300 million crowns for the first six months of 1997.

- Norwegian cruise liner NCL Holding has bought a cruiseship worth 180 million crowns from Germany's Deutsche Seereederei. During the last two years, the German cruise company liner has been forced by its creditors to sell most of its ships.
- Finansbanken sees a 20 percent correction in the Norwegian share market, and adds that it could fall as much as 25 to 30 percent. The bank says investors have been neglecting negative signals.
